I wouldn't dismiss psychedelic-induced revelations as idiocy. I think usually that when they make sense in the moment, there is probably some truth to them. The drug just may be freeing you from having to think in your usual terms, so you have some realization that is consistent but for which you don't have the ability to put it into language. My opinion though, is that, even if some of these realizations have some truth to them, is that this is relatively useless and masturbatory unless you are also spending a lot of your daily life learning the tools of the trade to actually evaluate and express your ideas. Unless you do, you will never be able to get any of it down on paper before you lose hold of the understanding that you momentarily had. It's possible that, if you had had the physics and math prerequisites during this episode, that you would later have been able to tease out exactly what you meant in formal terms that would make sense to other people. You might have found that you were just stating a philosophical interpretation of the current theories, or perhaps re-proposing a sketch of an existing theory.

Potheads like to use Carl Sagan as an example of a scientist who was pro-marijuana. It certainly doesn't make you a genius, but it could be of some use in moderation and when paired with hard work in the usual tools of the trade. If that's not your bag, though, I would say that even if you never make any use of these kind of incommunicable and vague revelations, they actually might not be completely masturbatory in that they can internally give you the sensation of understanding your own experience. I personally advocate using meditation as a way to reach these states and have these revelations, as you'll be less likely to dismiss them as some hallucination or artifact of the drug, and also that you won't have any memory impairment issue.
